source_title: Bethesda Officially Comments on Fallout 5 Gameplay Change
source_excerpt:
The wait for Fallout 5 has been a long one, but Bethesda is already making some important decisions about how its next trip to the wasteland will look and play. The last single-player mainline entry, Fallout 4 , arrived back in 2015, and quite a bit has changed in the gaming industry since then. Fortunately, the company isn't planning to build its next post-apocalyptic RPG using the same technology that powered Bethesda's classic games .
One of the biggest questions surrounding Fallout 5 is how much of a leap it will make over previous entries. Bethesda's RPGs have always been about freedom, but the technology behind those experiences has also faced plenty of criticism over the years. With Fallout 5 , Bethesda is looking to improve that technology while keeping the features that have made its games so popular.
Bethesda has confirmed that Fallout 5 will use Creation Engine 3, the latest version of the studio's proprietary game engine. Speaking with Windows Central, Bethesda's Todd Howard explained that the technology is about much more than improved graphics, with Bethesda placing considerable emphasis on the tools and systems used to build its massive open-world RPGs . According to Howard, those systems are particularly important when the development team comes up with ambitious ideas:
"For the kinds of worlds that we want to build....our designers ask for so much crazy stuff, and our tech team finds a way to do it. I think that's really defined our games where you feel like anything is possible."
For Fallout 5 , Creation Engine 3 could make a substantial difference to the overall experience. The franchise has always encouraged exploration, and Bethesda wants to keep that open-world freedom while giving its developers more advanced tools to work with. Of course, the new engine doesn't necessarily mean Fallout 5 will eliminate loading screens or feature a completely seamless world, nor does it mean it will completly revolutionize the gameplay. Still, it's an important upgrade for a franchise where exploration and interacting with the environment are such major parts of the experience.
Fallout 5 won't be the first Bethesda game to use Creation Engine 3. Bethesda confirmed that The Elder Scrolls 6 would use Creation Engine 3 first , which is the studio's current focus. Reports suggest that a full-blown reveal of TES6 , as well as its title, could happen next month to celebrate Skyrim 's 15-year anniversary .
Ultimately, there's still a long way to go before Fallout 5 is released, especially with Bethesda focusing much of its attention on The Elder Scrolls 6 . There's still years before Bethesda outright confirms Fallout 5's physical setting , too. However, the engine upgrade offers an early indication of how the studio intends to approach its next major post-apocalyptic RPG. Fallout 4 is already more than 10 years old, and expectations for its eventual successor will only continue growing.
